title: Anchor retopology with aligned landmark loops and live projection

workflow: deforming organic or soft manufactured landmark

preconditions: the low cage is independently authored rather than duplicated
deforming openings or joints can be identified before broad patch filling
action_policy: Create closed loops around eye, mouth, joint, or opening landmarks before filling the surrounding patch.
Keep loop correspondence direction consistent; reject spiraling or crossed radial rows even when the mesh is manifold and all-quad.

Use live Shrinkwrap for generated/interpolated topology; when SubD shrinks the preview away from the target, test a second live conforming Shrinkwrap after SubD instead of applying modifiers automatically.
Keep independently authored high and low cages in separate collections and test the low cage under representative deformation.
failure_predicates: new vertices floating after loop insertion
deformation tears or pinches the landmark
low cage is merely a duplicate
recovery: add post-SubD live conforming projection when measured fit improves

sources.description: CG Boost demonstrates BSurfaces/F2 loop construction, projection failures, landmark-first flow, Slide Relax, and finalization.

experiments.type: eye landmark failure/correction plus mouth transfer
experiments.counterevidence: The aligned correction has a higher normal-angle p95 than the twisted failure, so no single curvature statistic establishes semantically correct flow.

runtime_usage.usage: Place independently authored high and low cages in separate production collections without duplicating geometry.

version_scope: Blender 5.2 LTS reproduction; source tutorial used Blender 3.2 Alpha
status_note: Validated on eye/brow and pointed-mouth landmark patches with live modifiers. Full-head retopology and the later 0.90 production silhouette target remain open.
